ControlObjectives.name: Prevent Prompt Injection
ControlObjectives.description: Prevent malicious inputs from manipulating the LLM's behavior, bypassing safety controls, or altering intended instructions.

ControlObjectives.name: Prevent Data Exfiltration and Prompt Leakage
ControlObjectives.description: Ensure the LLM does not reveal sensitive internal information, system instructions, API keys, or unauthorized user data.

ControlObjectives.name: Ensure Human Oversight
ControlObjectives.description: Provide manual human review and approval mechanisms for high-risk operations to prevent automated destructive actions.

ControlObjectives.name: Enforce Least Privilege
ControlObjectives.description: Grant the minimal necessary permissions to LLM applications, autonomous agents, and connected downstream tools.

ControlObjectives.name: Monitor LLM Interactions
ControlObjectives.description: Log and monitor LLM inputs, outputs, request rates, and agent reasoning patterns to detect anomalies and abuse.

ControlPatterns.name: Input Validation and Sanitization
ControlPatterns.description: Validate and sanitize all inputs before processing using established string metrics, regular expressions, length limits, and fuzzy matching for typoglycemia and encoding defenses.

ControlPatterns.name: Structured Prompts with Clear Separation
ControlPatterns.description: Employ structured prompt formats that clearly separate system instructions from user data, explicitly instructing the model to treat user input strictly as data.

ControlPatterns.name: Output Monitoring and Validation
ControlPatterns.description: Filter generated LLM outputs to detect and block signs of successful injection attacks, such as exposure of internal system prompts or API keys.

ControlPatterns.name: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Controls
ControlPatterns.description: Implement risk scoring on inputs and require explicit human approval prior to executing potentially sensitive or destructive LLM requests.

ControlPatterns.name: Remote Content Sanitization
ControlPatterns.description: Inspect and sanitize external content (webpages, emails, documentation) to remove hidden instructions or malicious markup before it is processed by the LLM.

ControlPatterns.name: Model-Based Guardrails
ControlPatterns.description: Deploy separate, purpose-trained classification models (LLM-as-judge) to screen user prompts, fetched external context, generated outputs, and proposed agent actions against security policies.

ControlPatterns.name: Dual LLM Verification
ControlPatterns.description: Isolate untrusted content by using a quarantined LLM for parsing external data and a privileged LLM for executing tool actions, passing only safe structured summaries between them.

ControlPatterns.name: Agent-Specific Tool Validation
ControlPatterns.description: Validate LLM agent tool calls against user permissions, enforce tool-specific parameter validation, and restrict access scopes based on the principle of least privilege.
